thread.title: After the Bell: Dow Drops 81 Points as Apple Can’t Do the Heavy Lifting

author: Ben Levisohn
title: After the Bell: Dow Drops 81 Points as Apple Can’t Do the Heavy Lifting
text:
By Ben Levisohn Aug. 1, 2018 6:51 p.m. ET Apple's Day . Apple's (AAPL) big day couldn't lift the Dow Jones Industrial Average , which fell for the third time in four days. The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged , but indicated that there could be two more hikes this year. Tesla (TSLA) was soaring after releasing earnings after the close. In today's After the Bell , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...observe that stocks, gold, and Treasuries all fell today;
•...explain why Apple soared to the top of the S&P 500;
•...and highlight Hanesbrands' (HBI) tumble to the bottom of the index.
Everybody Hurts It was not a good day to be an investor...unless you owned Apple (AAPL).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 81.37 points, or 0.3%, to 25,333.82 on Wednesday. The S&P 500, meanwhile, dipped 0.1% to 2813.36. And stocks weren't the only thing that fell. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) also dipped 0.1%, to $118.34, while the SPDR Gold ETF (GLD) fell 0.7%, to $115.20.
It was, of course, Fed day . Though there wasn't much said by the Fed.
"There were very few changes in language from June 13, and the tone and content of the policy statement continue to point to gradual rate hikes going forward," writes Ward McCarthy , chief financial economist at Jefferies . "Based on the trajectory of the economy and the likelihood that inflation will be at or 'close to' the 2% dual mandate objective for months to come, we anticipate that the Fed will indeed implement four rates hikes in 2018, in September and December."
That message wasn't great for investors as the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF, and the SPDR Gold ETF. Each fell at least 0.1%, only the ninth time that's occurred on a Fed day, according to Sundial Capital's Jason Goepfert . Stocks have risen over the following 30 days on all nine occasions, Goepfert says, while gold has rallied just once. Treasuries did not have a direction over that time frame.
Let's hope the pattern repeats itself.
The Hot Stock Apple (AAPL) shot to the top of the S&P 500 today after it offered strong iPhone sales projections.
Shares of Apple were up 5.9%, or $11.21, to $ 201.5.
The stock just cracked the $200-per-share barrier today and is on course to be the first U.S. company to reach a $1 trillion market value . “Apple’s high-end portfolio held up well this quarter after the company indicated that the iPhone X was again the best-selling model,” said Jeffrey Kvaal , an analyst at Nomura Instinet .
The technology giant is up 19% year to date and 29.5% for the past year. — Varada Bhat

The Biggest Loser Hanesbrands (HBI) lost nearly one-fifth of its value after it missed earning estimates, making it the worst performer in the S&P 500 index.
The shares plunged 19%, or $4.3 to $17.96.
The company said it wasn’t renewing a contract with Target (TGT) to sell an exclusive line of C9 by Champion activewear. The current contract expires on January 2020. “In the past year, Hanesbrands took in about $380 million in sales from the C9 line,” Cowen analyst John Kernan wrote.
Shares of Hanesbrands were down 14.1% year to date and 24.6% for the past year. — V.B.
